chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The shroud (kafan) is taken from all the wealth (of the estate)."

key_terms.الْكَفَنُ: The shroud or burial cloth used to wrap the deceased.

ai.seo_question: Is the cost of the shroud paid from the deceased's estate before inheritance distribution?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing that the cost of the shroud (*kafan*) is a primary deduction from the deceased's total estate, payable before the distribution of shares to heirs. This principle underscores the priority of bodily dignity in Islamic jurisprudence, ensuring the deceased is buried with honor as a fundamental obligation settled from the general assets rather than specific bequests.
